cases.instruction: Student (studying chapter 4) asks: "What does the graph in figure 4.2 actually show?" Explain at standard level.

source_excerpts.text: Figure 4.2 plots the values of table 4.1 with current on the horizontal x-axis in amperes and voltage on the vertical y-axis in volts. The plotted points lie on a straight line passing through the origin. The line rises by 2 volts for every 1 ampere, so its slope is 2 volts per ampere.
Table 4.1, measured values for a single resistor. Column headings: current in amperes, voltage in volts. Row 1: 1 A, 2 V. Row 2: 2 A, 4 V. Row 3: 3 A, 6 V.

reference.text: Figure 4.2 plots voltage (volts, vertical y-axis) against current (amperes, horizontal x-axis) for the values in table 4.1. cases.instruction: Pending question: "Using table 4.1, what is the resistance?" The student answered "2 volts". Give feedback.

source_excerpts.text: Table 4.1, measured values for a single resistor. Column headings: current in amperes, voltage in volts. Row 1: 1 A, 2 V. Row 2: 2 A, 4 V. Row 3: 3 A, 6 V.

reference.text: The number 2 is right but the unit is wrong: resistance is R = V / I, for example 2 V / 1 A = 2 ohms. Volts measure voltage, not resistance.
